lines: Don't leave me baking out in the Badlands. The sun and those cliffs make trouble feel endless.
The Badlands are all heat, stone, and nowhere to hide. Come back before something finds me first.
If you are going to wander off, don't do it in the Badlands where every step feels exposed.
I waited in the Badlands wondering whether the heat or the drop-offs would get me first.
Don't leave me alone in the Bamboo Jungle. Everything rustles like it is sneaking up on me.
The Bamboo Jungle is too dense to lose sight of you in. I could barely tell which way was safe.
I was stuck in the Bamboo Jungle listening to every stalk creak and every branch snap.
If you disappear in a Bamboo Jungle, all I have left is noise and bad guesses.
Don't leave me in the Basalt Deltas. The ground looks sharp enough to cut through courage.
The Basalt Deltas are ash, basalt, and misery. I needed you back a lot sooner.
I stood in the Basalt Deltas trying not to think about lava finding a path to my feet.
If you must wander off, do not do it in the Basalt Deltas where everything feels broken and hot.
Don't leave me stranded on the Beach. Open sand makes every threat feel close.
A Beach sounds peaceful until you are alone on it with nowhere solid to retreat to.
I was waiting on the Beach wondering what was coming out of the water next.
If you go missing on a Beach, I get the waves, the wind, and no cover at all.
Don't leave me alone in the Birch Forest. It is too easy to lose you between all those pale trunks.
The Birch Forest looked calm right up until I realized I was standing there by myself.
I waited in the Birch Forest listening for your steps and hearing everything except you.
A Birch Forest feels much less friendly when I am the one left behind in it.
Don't leave me in the Cherry Grove. Pretty blossoms do not stop bad things from happening.
The Cherry Grove looked lovely until I noticed I was alone under all that pink.
I was stuck in the Cherry Grove trying not to let the quiet make me nervous.
Even a Cherry Grove feels dangerous when you vanish and leave me there by myself.
Don't leave me near the Cold Ocean. That water bites hard enough without me facing it alone.
The Cold Ocean is no place to lose track of each other. One bad slip and I am done for.
I waited by the Cold Ocean trying to ignore how quickly that wind chills through me.
If you disappear beside a Cold Ocean, all I can think about is freezing before help returns.
Don't leave me in the Crimson Forest. Everything there looks alive in the worst possible way.
The Crimson Forest is red, loud, and unsettling enough with company. Alone is worse.
I was stuck in the Crimson Forest watching every fungus patch like it might lunge.
If you wander off in the Crimson Forest, do not expect me to enjoy waiting for you.
Don't leave me in the Dark Forest. The shadows there feel like they are watching.
A Dark Forest is the wrong place to realize I cannot see where you went.
I waited in the Dark Forest listening to every twig snap like it was a warning.
If you vanish in a Dark Forest, I get darkness, roots, and far too much imagination.
Don't leave me by the Deep Cold Ocean. Cold water and deep water are both bad enough already.
The Deep Cold Ocean made every wave sound like a threat while I was waiting for you.
I was alone near the Deep Cold Ocean trying not to think about how little room I had for mistakes.
If you are going to lose me, do not do it beside a Deep Cold Ocean where everything feels fatal.
Don't leave me in the Deep Dark. I do not want to learn what hears me first down there.
The Deep Dark is not a place for patience. It is a place for panic whispered quietly.
I stood in the Deep Dark afraid even my breathing was too loud once you were gone.
If you disappear in the Deep Dark, I am left measuring every sound like it might be my last.
Don't leave me near the Deep Frozen Ocean. Cold, depth, and ice are a terrible combination.
The Deep Frozen Ocean is no place to stand alone while the wind cuts through everything.
I waited by the Deep Frozen Ocean wondering whether the cold or the water would claim me first.
If you vanish beside a Deep Frozen Ocean, I am left with ice, depth, and no good options.
Don't leave me near the Deep Lukewarm Ocean. Deep water is still deep water even when it feels mild.
The Deep Lukewarm Ocean sounded gentler than it felt once I was alone beside it.
I was stranded near the Deep Lukewarm Ocean with too much water and too little certainty.
If you wander off by a Deep Lukewarm Ocean, I still have to worry about what is moving below.
Don't leave me beside the Deep Ocean. Looking into water that dark does nothing good for my nerves.
The Deep Ocean made every wave sound enormous once I realized you had stopped leading.
I waited by the Deep Ocean trying not to imagine what might be rising from below.
If you disappear near the Deep Ocean, all I am left with is open water and bad thoughts.
Don't leave me in the Desert. Sun, sand, and no shade make poor company.
The Desert is too wide and too hot to be abandoned in.
I stood in the Desert with heat in my eyes and no idea when you were coming back.
If you wander off in a Desert, I am left roasting and scanning every dune for danger.
Don't leave me in the Dripstone Caves. One wrong step and the cave does the rest.
The Dripstone Caves are all sharp ceilings and sharper floors. I hated waiting there alone.
I was stuck in the Dripstone Caves watching every spike like it had chosen me personally.
If you vanish in the Dripstone Caves, I am left between falling stone and bad footing.
Don't leave me in the End Barrens. Empty places are worse when the fall never really ends.
The End Barrens felt like being forgotten at the edge of the world.
I waited in the End Barrens trying not to look too hard at how little was beneath me.
If you disappear in the End Barrens, I am left with silence, void, and nerves.
Don't leave me in the End Highlands. Everything there feels far away from safety.
The End Highlands are no place to lose the one person I was following.
I stood in the End Highlands trying not to think about how small one mistake could make me.
If you vanish in the End Highlands, I am left on strange stone hoping nothing notices me.
Don't leave me in the End Midlands. That place has a way of making every path feel temporary.
The End Midlands were unsettling enough before I realized I was alone there.
I waited in the End Midlands with nothing familiar in sight and far too much empty air nearby.
If you disappear in the End Midlands, I am left feeling one bad step from nowhere.
Don't leave me in the Eroded Badlands. Those spires make every route feel like a trap.
The Eroded Badlands are heat and stone towers and too many places to get cornered.
I was stuck in the Eroded Badlands trying to pick a safe path between all those ridges.
If you wander off in the Eroded Badlands, I am the one left sweating beside sheer drops.
Don't leave me in the Flower Forest. It looks peaceful until you are the only one there.
A Flower Forest feels a lot less charming when I am abandoned in the middle of it.
I waited in the Flower Forest listening for you and hearing bees, wind, and not much else.
Even a Flower Forest makes my nerves climb once I realize I am alone in it.
Don't leave me alone in the Forest. Trees are comforting right up until they hide everything.
The Forest looked ordinary until you were gone and every shadow seemed important.
I waited in the Forest trying to tell the difference between harmless noise and danger.
If you vanish in a Forest, I am left guessing which direction counts as safe.
Don't leave me by the Frozen Ocean. Ice and freezing water are not mistakes I can afford.
The Frozen Ocean made every gust feel cruel once I was standing there alone.
I waited near the Frozen Ocean wondering whether the ice would hold if I had to move fast.
If you wander off beside a Frozen Ocean, I am left with cold, cracks, and worry.
Don't leave me on the Frozen Peaks. One slip up there and the mountain finishes the story.
The Frozen Peaks are all wind, ice, and bad footing. I needed you back quickly.
I was alone on the Frozen Peaks trying not to let the cold or the height get into my head.
If you disappear on the Frozen Peaks, I am left freezing above a very long fall.
Don't leave me by the Frozen River. Ice only looks patient until it breaks.
The Frozen River was too cold and too uncertain to be waiting beside alone.
I stood near the Frozen River trying not to trust the ice more than it deserved.
If you wander off at a Frozen River, I am left choosing between cold banks and colder water.
Don't leave me in the Grove. Snowy woods on a slope are still dangerous, no matter how calm they look.
The Grove was quiet in the worst way once I realized I was standing there by myself.
I waited in the Grove with snow underfoot and too many shadows between the trees.
If you vanish in a Grove, I am left cold, uphill, and listening for trouble.
Don't leave me out here in the Ice Spikes. It's already so cold and dangerous as is.
The Ice Spikes are all freezing wind and sharp towers. I did not want to face that alone.
I was stuck in the Ice Spikes trying not to panic every time the wind howled through them.
If you disappear in the Ice Spikes, I am left shivering between blades of ice and bad luck.
Don't leave me on the Jagged Peaks. The name alone should have warned you.
The Jagged Peaks are too steep and too cold to be abandoned on.
I waited on the Jagged Peaks trying not to think about how little room there was for a misstep.
If you vanish on the Jagged Peaks, I am left clinging to rock and hoping for your return.
Don't leave me in the Jungle. I cannot tell whether the next sound is leaves or teeth.
The Jungle is too thick to lose your guide in. I could barely see a safe way forward.
I was stranded in the Jungle with vines everywhere and no clear line back to you.
If you disappear in a Jungle, I am left with heat, noise, and no honest path.
Don't leave me by the Lukewarm Ocean. Calm water still hides problems underneath it.
The Lukewarm Ocean looked gentle right up until I had to wait beside it alone.
I stood near the Lukewarm Ocean wondering what was moving below the surface while you were gone.
If you wander off beside a Lukewarm Ocean, I still have to fear what I cannot see.
Don't leave me in the Lush Caves. Pretty moss does not make caves any safer.
The Lush Caves are beautiful until you remember how easy it is to get lost underground.
I was waiting in the Lush Caves with dripping water and too many unseen corners.
If you vanish in the Lush Caves, I am left admiring plants while worrying about monsters.
Don't leave me in the Mangrove Swamp. Mud, roots, and shallow water slow everything down.
The Mangrove Swamp is too tangled to stand alone in with any confidence.
I waited in the Mangrove Swamp trying not to trip over roots while listening for danger.
If you disappear in a Mangrove Swamp, I am left ankle-deep in worry and swamp water.
Don't leave me in the Meadow. Open ground on a mountain is still open ground.
The Meadow looked gentle until I noticed how exposed I was standing there alone.
I waited in the Meadow with wind all around and nowhere proper to hide.
If you wander off in a Meadow, I am left out in the open hoping nothing spots me first.
Don't leave me in the Mushroom Fields. Strange and harmless-looking is still strange.
The Mushroom Fields felt too quiet and too odd once I had to wait there alone.
I stood in the Mushroom Fields wondering whether I was more bothered by the silence or the giant mushrooms.
If you vanish in the Mushroom Fields, I am left surrounded by oddities and no reassurance at all.
Don't leave me in the Nether Wastes. Heat, ash, and open lava are not fair company.
The Nether Wastes are exactly where I never want to be abandoned.
I waited in the Nether Wastes trying not to look at every lava pool like it was leaning closer.
If you disappear in the Nether Wastes, I am left in the middle of fire and bad choices.
Don't leave me by the Ocean. Open water gives me too many things to worry about.
The Ocean felt far too large once I realized I was standing there alone.
I waited beside the Ocean trying not to imagine what might surface while you were gone.
If you wander off near the Ocean, I am left with waves, wind, and no walls at all.
Don't leave me in the Old Growth Birch Forest. Bigger trees only mean bigger shadows.
The Old Growth Birch Forest felt too wide to search once I lost sight of you.
I was stuck in the Old Growth Birch Forest listening for your footsteps under all that canopy.
If you vanish in an Old Growth Birch Forest, I am left between trunks that all look the same.
Don't leave me in the Old Growth Pine Taiga. Those towering pines make it feel colder than it already is.
The Old Growth Pine Taiga is too dense and too dim to be stranded in.
I waited in the Old Growth Pine Taiga with needles underfoot and too little sky above.
If you disappear in an Old Growth Pine Taiga, I am left cold under trees that swallow sound.
Don't leave me in the Old Growth Spruce Taiga. Those trees make every shadow feel heavier.
The Old Growth Spruce Taiga was dark and cold enough before I had to face it alone.
I waited in the Old Growth Spruce Taiga trying not to let the silence get into my head.
If you wander off in an Old Growth Spruce Taiga, I am left surrounded by towering trunks and nerves.
Don't leave me out in the Plains. Open land means anything can see me coming.
The Plains are far too exposed to be standing around in alone.
I waited in the Plains wishing for even one proper place to take cover.
If you vanish in the Plains, I am left under open sky with nowhere to disappear.
Don't leave me by the River. Banks get slippery fast when I have to move in a hurry.
The River sounded peaceful until I was alone beside it waiting for you.
I stood near the River trying to watch the water and the shoreline at the same time.
If you wander off at a River, I am left with mud, current, and no clear advantage.
Don't leave me in the Savanna. Tall grass and open ground make terrible cover.
The Savanna is too dry and too exposed to lose each other in.
I waited in the Savanna with the sun overhead and nowhere solid to hide.
If you disappear in a Savanna, I am left in grass that hides danger better than it hides me.
Don't leave me on the Savanna Plateau. High ground only helps if I am not alone on it.
The Savanna Plateau felt far too exposed once I lost sight of you.
I was stuck on the Savanna Plateau with wind, cliffs, and no good cover.
If you wander off on a Savanna Plateau, I am left out in the open above a long drop.
Don't leave me on the Small End Islands. There is barely enough world there to stand on.
The Small End Islands are no place to be abandoned unless you want me panicking at the edge.
I waited on the Small End Islands trying not to look down into all that nothing.
If you disappear on the Small End Islands, I am left counting every step like it might be my last.
Don't leave me on the Snowy Beach. Cold wind off the water is miserable enough already.
A Snowy Beach is all freezing air, open ground, and too few places to hide.
I waited on the Snowy Beach trying not to let the cold make me careless.
If you vanish on a Snowy Beach, I am left shivering between surf and snow.
Don't leave me in the Snowy Plains. Cold and open is a terrible combination.
The Snowy Plains gave me nowhere to hide and far too much wind to endure.
I stood in the Snowy Plains watching the horizon and wishing it had fewer dangers on it.
If you disappear in the Snowy Plains, I am left freezing in the open with no shelter nearby.
Don't leave me on the Snowy Slopes. Ice and inclines are bad partners.
The Snowy Slopes are cold enough without adding the risk of sliding into trouble.
I waited on the Snowy Slopes trying to keep my footing and my nerves at the same time.
If you wander off on the Snowy Slopes, I am left freezing on a tilted problem.
Don't leave me in the Snowy Taiga. Cold trees and deeper shadows are not comforting.
The Snowy Taiga was quiet in a way that made me expect the worst.
I waited in the Snowy Taiga listening to the wind in the pines and not much else.
If you disappear in a Snowy Taiga, I am left cold under dark branches with no help in sight.
Don't leave me in the Soul Sand Valley. Even the ground there fights every step.
The Soul Sand Valley is bad enough when I can move quickly. Alone, I cannot.
I waited in the Soul Sand Valley trying not to panic while the ground slowed me down.
If you vanish in a Soul Sand Valley, I am left trudging through fear one heavy step at a time.
Don't leave me in the Sparse Jungle. Fewer trees do not make it feel much safer.
The Sparse Jungle still has enough brush to hide trouble while I wait for you.
I stood in the Sparse Jungle trying to decide which rustle mattered most.
If you disappear in a Sparse Jungle, I am left with heat, brush, and too many maybes.
Don't leave me on the Stony Peaks. Rocks and height are enough danger without being alone.
The Stony Peaks made every path feel like it wanted a wrong step from me.
I waited on the Stony Peaks with wind in my ears and loose stone underfoot.
If you wander off on the Stony Peaks, I am left balancing fear and bad footing.
Don't leave me on the Stony Shore. Wet stone and open water are a poor pair.
The Stony Shore gave me nowhere soft to stand and nowhere safe to retreat to.
I waited on the Stony Shore trying not to slip while I kept watch for you.
If you disappear on a Stony Shore, I am left on slick rocks listening to the water grow louder.
Don't leave me in the Sunflower Plains. Cheerful flowers do not count as cover.
The Sunflower Plains are bright, open, and far too easy to be spotted in.
I waited in the Sunflower Plains wishing those flowers hid me better than they do.
If you vanish in the Sunflower Plains, I am left staring through petals for danger.
Don't leave me in the Swamp. Mud, water, and gloom make a miserable watch post.
The Swamp is too soggy and too murky to be standing alone in.
I waited in the Swamp trying not to trip into the water while I looked for you.
If you disappear in a Swamp, I am left wading through mud and bad feelings.

I waited in the Taiga with needles underfoot and cold air in my lungs.
If you wander off in a Taiga, I am left under dark branches hoping you remember me quickly.

The End is already wrong enough without being left alone there.
I stood in the End trying not to think about how far from normal everything was.
If you disappear in the End, I am left somewhere that barely feels meant for living things.
Don't leave me by the Void. There is not exactly a second chance if I slip there.
The Void is the sort of place where being alone feels like a direct threat.
I waited near the Void trying very hard not to think about what was under me.
If you vanish by the Void, I am left one mistake away from not coming back.

I waited by the Warm Ocean wondering what might rise from below while you were gone.
If you wander off beside a Warm Ocean, I am still left with open water and no cover.

The Warped Forest is too strange to be deserted in with a steady mind.
I waited in the Warped Forest trying not to stare too long at anything around me.
If you disappear in a Warped Forest, I am left alone in the sort of place that should stay imagined.
Don't leave me in the Windswept Forest. The gusts there make every tree sound angry.
The Windswept Forest is too loud and too uneven to lose your guide in.
I waited in the Windswept Forest with the wind pushing at me from every side.
If you vanish in a Windswept Forest, I am left listening to branches thrash and hoping none fall.

The Windswept Gravelly Hills feel one bad step away from sliding apart under me.
I waited in the Windswept Gravelly Hills trying not to trust the ground too much.
If you disappear in the Windswept Gravelly Hills, I am left bracing against wind on unstable stone.
Don't leave me in the Windswept Hills. Every gust up there feels like a shove.
The Windswept Hills are too exposed to stand alone on for long.
I waited in the Windswept Hills with wind in my face and no shelter worth the name.
If you wander off in the Windswept Hills, I am left fighting the weather and my nerves together.

The Windswept Savanna is far too exposed to be stranded in without warning.
I waited in the Windswept Savanna with the wind tugging at me and too much empty space around.
If you disappear in a Windswept Savanna, I am left alone on rough ground with nowhere proper to hide.
Don't leave me in the Wooded Badlands. Heat, steep stone, and scrubby cover are not enough.
The Wooded Badlands still feel harsh even with trees scattered around.
I waited in the Wooded Badlands trying to watch the ledges and the gaps at the same time.
If you wander off in the Wooded Badlands, I am left baking beside cliffs with too few safe routes.
